title: Lords of Thunder
subtitle: A knight flying into heavy metal
summary: Lords of Thunder is Red Company's fantasy shooting game, released for TurboDuo in North America in March 1993 and in Japan as Winds of Thunder that April.
body: Lords of Thunder is Red Company's fantasy shooting game, released for TurboDuo in North America in March 1993 and in Japan as Winds of Thunder that April. The armored knight Landis flies through scrolling stages to confront the dark forces threatening Mistral. Elemental armor changes his weapons, while a forceful recorded rock score accompanies the battle. The mixture gives a familiar shooter structure a different personality: the central figure is a flying warrior, and the next choice begins before he enters the stage.

The first six stages can be tackled in a chosen order. Before each one, the player selects armor associated with an element, changing Landis's shots and bombs. His sword also threatens nearby enemies, rewarding careful proximity as well as distant firing. Large bosses close the stages, while power crystals strengthen the attack along the way. Damage reduces both health and firepower, so surviving a difficult passage concerns the strength available for the next encounter too. Clearing the six routes opens the final stage of the campaign.

Enemies drop colored crystals that serve as money in the shop between stages. The player can buy bombs, protective items and health-restoring supplies, turning a successful run into preparation for another battle. Satoshi Miyashita of T's Music composed the soundtrack, and Masamune Shirow illustrated the cover. The development team included former Technosoft staff with experience on Thunder Force. That background carries into the brisk shooting, while the elemental equipment, shop and hard-rock accompaniment establish the particular character of this CD-based adventure.
